thread.title: EBay Will Finally Start Paying a Dividend. It Only Took 24 Years

author: Barron's
title: EBay Will Finally Start Paying a Dividend. It Only Took 24 Years
text:
Photograph by Daniel Acker/Bloomberg After 24 years, eBay (ticker: EBAY ) will start paying a dividend.
The e-tailer earned 71 cents a share on a continuing-operations basis in last year's fourth quarter, three cents above the consensus, according to FactSet.
But a potentially much more important development was eBay's announcement on Wednesday that it has initiated a quarterly dividend of 14 cents a share. The move could help support a stock that has done better recently but is still off 16% over the past year. Shares were trading Wednesday morning at $33.30, down 1.2%.
The Back Story
Like many technology companies, eBay-which was founded in 1995-didn't pay a dividend for many years. It's typical of younger firms to refrain from paying a dividend to fund growth initiatives. A dividend launch typically occurs after a company matures and its growth trajectory slows down.
Read more: Elliott Associates Wants Big Changes at eBay
But this dynamic has been changing in the world of tech stocks, as Barron's pointed out last fall ( "6 Tech Stocks With Solid Dividends," Sept. 21, 2018). Among the legacy tech companies that have initiated dividends are Apple ( AAPL ), which did so in 2012; Cisco Systems ( CSCO ), 2011; Intel ( INTC ), 1992; Microsoft ( MSFT ), 2003; and Oracle ( ORCL ), 2009.
The Plot Twist
EBay is the latest example of this trend. Besides initiating a quarterly dividend of 14 cents a share this week, the company announced it will expand its share repurchase authorization by $4 billion.
"We are confident in the strength of our business and future growth prospects, as demonstrated by our decision to institute eBay's first-ever dividend and increase our share repurchase program," Devin Wenig , president and CEO of eBay, said in a statement.
https://asset.barrons.com/dj-mg/dice/barrons-staffpicks-2d590600-c862-4394-b9d3-66b48c376d60/inset.json
This could mark a turn in how the stock is viewed by investors. EBay "looks more appealing to value investors focused on income rather than to growth oriented tech investors," asserts a Jefferies research note.
Moving Forward
As an income vehicle, the stock would have some appeal. On an annual basis, the stock's yield will be about 1.6%-not shabby, but below the S&P 500 's average of about 2%. Microsoft yields 1.8%, while Cisco is at 2.9%.
But initiating a dividend may not please all investors.
"While an accelerated capital return plan highlights confidence in cash flow generation, we would prefer a greater focus on internal investments to rejuvenate the core business," Jefferies maintains.
